item.title: Are Iran and Ukraine wars getting tangled in Caspian Sea?
item.description: Tehran has threatened a response after a Ukrainian strike on an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea that Kyiv says was carrying weapons to Russia. Still, Ukraine says it wants to avoid escalation with Tehran.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Spain will send troops to Ceuta to help with border security
item.description: Authorities in the Spanish city of Ceuta asked Madrid to declare a national emergency and send military assistance. Crowds of people breached the border of the territory next to Morocco as police lost control.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Epstein files: How victims remain exposed to identification
item.description: US officials vowed to revise redactions after files exposed information that identified survivors of sexual abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. A DW investigation found that sensitive information remains online.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Human trafficking in Mexico: the dark side of tourism
item.description: By May, a record-breaking 20 million tourists had visited Mexico so far in 2026. But with increased tourism comes a heightened risk of human trafficking and sexual exploitation. Women and children are most vulnerable.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: How crypto miners are stealing power in Southeast Asia
item.description: Across Southeast Asia, illegal cryptocurrency miners are stealing vast amounts of electricity, straining national grids and exposing links to organized crime.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Crete wildfires cause evacuations and firefighter deaths
item.description: Wildfires on the Greek island of Crete are forcing thousands of residents and tourists to evacuate. Three firefighters have died as Greece becomes the latest country, after France and Spain, to face summer blazes.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: French student fined over Singapore straw licking prank
item.description: A social media stunt involving a single straw has left a French student facing a hefty fine — and possible consequences for his right to remain in Singapore.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: How well are LGBTQ+ rights protected across Europe?
item.description: After the attack on Berlin’s Pride event on Saturday, the situation of the LGBTQ+ community in Germany is a topic of conversation. How well are queer rights protected in other European countries? An overview.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran war: Egypt's difficult balancing act
item.description: The US-Iran war has already had a negative economic impact on Egypt. Now new threats from the Houthi group in Yemen are likely to worsen that. At the same time, Egypt is trying to stay on good terms with all parties.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: How a Ugandan lost 20 years of her life to xenophobia
item.description: After decades of building lives in South Africa, hundreds of African migrants were forced to leave by renewed anti-immigrant tensions. A Ugandan who spent two decades in South Africa shared with DW how she's coping.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran signals gas price hike as fuel crisis looms
item.description: Iranian authorities want to dampen fuel consumption, but a sudden increase in gasoline prices risks social unrest as many Iranian households are already under severe economic pressure.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Lebanon's pilot zone plan: Can it work?
item.description: The Israeli army has handed so-called "pilot zones" back to the Lebanese, The move is meant to facilitate an end to fighting between Hezbollah and Israel, and to Israeli occupation. But locals and experts are skeptical.
